paper.title: Algorithm 747: Fortran subroutine to solve the eigenvalue assignment problem (staircase reduction and eigenvalue assignment)

field: numerics (linear systems and control: eigenvalue assignment by state feedback)
stack: Fortran 77 (TOMS 747 archive 747.gz: a shar of 36 files, with ddemo.f, dstair.f, dmevas.f, blas.f, lapack.f, eispk.f and makefile; test01.dat and dlog.ref)

claim.text: ddemo (double precision) on the shipped test01.dat (n=11, m=7) prints the computed gain matrix F; entry F(1,1) = 1.2366 and F(1,2) = -0.0621 (the first row, first two entries), as printed in the shipped dlog.ref. Absolute tolerance 5e-5 (the 4-decimal print half-unit), fixed in the queue entry before any run.

values.name: F(1,1) of test01, ddemo double precision (dlog.ref)

attempt: Reproduced at the registered claim (tol_abs 5e-5). Both passes (clean rebuilds of the unpacked tree with the authors' makefile target make ddemo, each run on test01.dat) give F(1,1) = 1.2366 and F(1,2) = -0.0621, matching the shipped dlog.ref block at its printed precision. The printed values are 4 decimals, so agreement is at the print resolution (the claim tolerance is the half-unit). The archive as shipped did not build: the makefile calls f77, which is absent from the host and the sandbox (make: f77: No such file or directory, build_exit=2). The fix was a compiler alias f77 -> gfortran (conda-forge) placed outside the tree; no source or build file was edited (build-only, manifests pre, mid and post compared). The shipped eigenvalue lists of the closed loop were not used as the claim (the queue entry says the two shipped logs disagree there).

original_attempt.reason: make ddemo stops at the first compile (ddemo.f, line makefile:29): f77 is not installed on the host or in the sandbox, so the archive as shipped does not build.
